Alright, I've just finished writing the core frontend files—`index.html`, `style.css`, and `app.js`—as well as updating the backend `app.py`. The new code reflects the design direction we discussed: an orange Hugging Face theme, proper Discord‑style UI components, and a richer JavaScript state model for handling Discord view, search, and fun‑facts modes.

Before I proceed to any further integration steps (like wiring up the FastAPI routes or testing the UI in a browser), I need to make sure the files I've just written are syntactically valid. A syntax error in `app.py` would cause the FastAPI server to crash on startup, and a JavaScript syntax error would prevent the client bundle from loading, leading to a broken UI. Since I don't have a live server running yet, the quickest way to catch any glaring issues is to run static syntax checks.

For Python, the standard tool is `python3 -m py_compile`. It will try to compile the file to bytecode and will raise an error if there’s any syntax problem. I’ll point it at `app.py`, which lives in the project root (`/home/lane/Blindbot/hf_space/app.py`). The command `python3 -m py_compile app.py` will suffice.

For JavaScript, Node provides a lint‑style syntax check via `node --check`. This will parse the file and report any syntax errors without actually executing the code. My `app.js` lives under the `static` folder, so the appropriate path is `static/app.js`.

I want a single command that runs both checks and gives me a clear indication of success. By chaining them with `&&`, the second check will only run if the first succeeds. Finally, appending `&& echo OK` will print a simple “OK” message if both steps pass, making it easy to confirm everything is fine in one go.

Thus, the Bash command I need to execute is:

```
python3 -m py_compile app.py && node --check static/app.js && echo OK
```

I’ll use the `Bash` tool to run this command, providing a brief description so the tool knows the intent (syntax‑checking both the backend and frontend). This will give me immediate feedback on any syntax errors before I move on to runtime testing or UI polishing.
